newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power higher as October approaches.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power higher as October approaches.

text.p: U.S spot power prices increased Monday as market participants scrambled to complete October business amid lingering power plant outages.
"Physical prices seem to be up in line with a bit of a short-squeeze for October," said one trader.
California-Oregon border power for Tuesday was last quoted $20.00-21.00 per megawatt hour, up from $17.50-18.00 for Friday's next-day quotes.
The market was also supported by higher Bonneville Power Administration price offers as well as the agency's move to separate the price of power from transmission.
Including transmission prices, BPA offered Tuesday COB at $23.27 per MWh.
"I don't think prices can stay this high," said a California trader. "At $22.00, more thermal units would come on line."
Next-day Palo Verde was last quoted $21.00-22.00, compared with $20.00-21.00 on Monday. Some sources reported PV offers as high as $26.00 for Tuesday.
October COB was last quoted $16.90-17.25 per MWh, up from $16.50-17.00 on Friday. Palo Verde for October was last quoted $17.20-17.45, up from $17.00-17.20.
Traders also said lingering plant outages, particulary at the San Onofre nuclear plant in California, were helping keep prices firm.
The 1,080 MW SONGS unit is not expected to be back up until October.
Several Northwest coal-fired units which were out of service last week were back in operation, but were expected to take a couple of days to reach full power.
In addition, Montana Power said one of the four 750 MW units at the Colstrip power plant was shut Satuday due to a tube leak and was scheduled to restart early Tuesday.
Sources familiar with operations at the Centralia coal-fired plant in Washington state and the Jim Bridger plant in Wyoming said Monday that units there were back on line.
A 790 MW unit at the Mohave power plant in Nevada was said to be in restart mode early Monday after tripping off on Wednesday.
